claims.claim: PromptKit's session recording system captures, stores, and replays LLM conversations
Recordings capture precise, millisecond-accurate event timestamps
Recordings capture all messages, tool calls, and media
Recordings contain enough information to replay conversations exactly

Diagram edge: Event Store (JSONL) feeds the Recording (Replay)
Diagram edge: Live Session emits real-time events
Diagram edge: Event Store writes to persistent storage
Diagram edge: Recording produces synchronized playback

FileEventStore persists events in JSONL (JSON Lines) format
JSONL event store lines have top-level fields seq and event, with event.type set to message.created
JSONL event store event payloads carry a timestamp field
Event type audio.output is a valid JSONL event type
FileEventStore storage is append-only and safe for concurrent writes
FileEventStore storage is streamable, processable without loading the whole file
FileEventStore storage is human-readable JSON per line
SessionRecording export format first line has type metadata with session_id, start_time and duration fields
SessionRecording event lines have type event, offset (e.g. "100ms") and event_type fields
The recording loader auto-detects both the FileEventStore JSONL and SessionRecording JSONL formats
recording.Load(path) loads a recording file and returns (rec, err)

Recording CPU overhead is minimal because events are queued and written asynchronously
Recording memory is bounded because segments are written incrementally
Input audio is 16kHz, 16-bit mono (~32KB per second)
Output audio is 24kHz, 16-bit mono (~48KB per second)
Base64 encoding adds roughly 33% overhead to stored audio
A 5-minute voice conversation generates approximately 24MB of raw audio
A 5-minute voice conversation generates approximately 32MB of JSONL with metadata
Recording can be disabled for CI or quick validation runs
JSONL recordings compress to a 70-80% reduction
Recordings support retention policies that auto-delete old recordings
Recording can be enabled selectively for specific scenarios

A duplex recording holds the provider audio.output events, which fill the assistant audio track; a text run whose provider returns no audio has no audio track
Arena runs every pack eval trigger at conversation end (turn triggers per assistant turn, then session, then on_conversation_complete), text and duplex alike
The duplex recording stages sit after the pack guardrail stage, so a recorded turn holds the enforced content
An Arena recording holds message.created, stream.interrupted and audio.output; Arena pipelines never produce audio.input, message.text.delta, image or video events
